transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I can’t shake this feeling that I’m a burden to everyone around me and that I’ve let my whole community down. My daughter finally persuaded me to come in and get some help because she's been so worried about me.
Have you felt this way for most of the past two years, or did this current period of feeling down begin more recently?

It's not brand new, no. It started about a year and a half ago when my divorce process began, and for a little over a year now, this heavy, hopeless feeling has been hanging over me almost the entire time.

During this past year, have there been any periods of a few weeks or longer where your symptoms were significantly more intense, perhaps including changes in your appetite, sleep patterns, or feeling completely unable to function?

Yes, it’s been a heavy, ongoing struggle for over a year now rather than just short phases. I’ve had to force myself to eat to the point where my clothes are loose, and I’ve let my chores, bills, and work shifts slide because everything feels so overwhelming.
Before this difficult year and a half began, did you experience any distinct periods in your life where you felt this same level of severe depression and inability to function?

No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. These feelings of severe depression and not being able to function are completely new to me. They only started when my marriage fell apart about a year and a half ago.
Looking back at your life before this current period, were there ever any other times where you felt depressed, even if it wasn't as severe as what you are experiencing now?
No, I don't recall having any other periods of depression before this. This is really the first time in my life I've ever felt this way.

During this past year, have there been any specific times where you felt completely unable to perform your daily tasks or care for yourself, or has your ability to function been consistently low throughout the entire period?

It has been consistently low and heavy throughout the entire past year, rather than just happening in short bursts. I've let my apartment and bills slide to the point where my daughter has to check in on me to make sure I'm keeping up with basic things. I’ve also missed quite a few of my crossing guard shifts or had to leave early because I just couldn't manage to get through them.

Over the past year, have there been any two-week periods where you felt essentially no moments of happiness or pleasure at all, or have you still been able to experience brief moments of relief or positive emotion?

Yes, there have been long stretches—well over two weeks at a time—where I felt absolutely no happiness or pleasure. It feels like the light has completely gone out inside of me and this gray cloud never really lifts. I'm just going through the motions every day without any moments of real relief.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have slowed down significantly, or conversely, that you feel unable to sit still and feel restless because of your inner agitation?

Yes, my body feels like it's constantly moving through mud, and I find myself shuffling across the street much slower than I used to. It also takes me a few long seconds just to get the words out when someone asks me a simple question.

Looking back at the entire period since your divorce began, have you experienced any distinct episodes where your symptoms became notably worse or more severe for at least two weeks, or has your mood been consistently low and unchanging the whole time?

The low mood, guilt, and feeling like a burden have been hanging over me almost the entire time since the divorce started. There was a brief period last fall where my sadness eased up a bit and I wasn't crying as much, but even during those weeks, the voices and the feeling of being watched were still fully present.
You mentioned hearing voices and feeling like you were being watched; do these experiences happen only when you are feeling at your most depressed, or do they occur at other times as well?

They actually happen even when I'm not feeling at my most depressed. Last fall, my sadness had eased a little and I wasn't crying during my shifts, but I still heard that man's voice criticizing me. I was also still convinced the school district was secretly collecting evidence to prove I was unfit to be around the kids.
